title: Transit, absorption, secretion boundary and faecal output for a healthy adult gut (task 5562, LN-4 {R-TRANSIT})
source: Abstracts and pages listed in sources.json under TR-* keys, plus EXC-* rows carried from task 3016. Several pages returned HTTP 403 or a browser check; where a figure comes from search-result text the Note says relayed. A null Value, Low and High means no opened page gave the figure; rows with Low and High and a null Value are ranges with no central value. Rows marked derived are my arithmetic.
rows: Mean human small intestinal transit time from pooled literature data
Statistical pooling of published transit-time data (studies and subjects not on the record)

95% confidence interval of 7 min on the mean (a pooling uncertainty, not a between-person spread; whether +/- 7 or a width of 7 is not stated). The compartmental transit and dispersion models fitted the flow profile; the single-compartment model did not.
Transit rate constant per compartment of a 7-compartment transit chain (derived)
7 equal compartments with mean total 199 min

My arithmetic (level 5): 7/199 = 0.0352 per min = 28.4 min per compartment. The count of 7 is relayed from a secondary page (the Huang, Lee and Yu 2009 review text opened does not state a count, and the Yu 1996 abstract does not either).
Compartmental absorption and transit model equation (Y_n, K_t, K_a)

Value null: the equation is an image on the page opened, so its exact form is not read here. The text defines Y_n as percent of dose in compartment n, K_t the transit rate constant, K_a the absorption rate constant, with absorption from stomach and colon taken as minor, passive and linear.
Small intestinal transit time across ingestible-capsule studies in healthy volunteers
Systematic review: 22 studies, 1,885 healthy volunteers; 17 studies reported gastric emptying and small intestinal times
A range of study results, no pooled mean. The authors state the times, above all gastric emptying, depend on the protocol.
Colonic transit time across ingestible-capsule studies
Whole gut transit time across ingestible-capsule studies
Range of study results. Gastric emptying time in the same review spans 0.4 to 15.3 h.
Small intestinal transit time, healthy controls, electromagnetic capsule
28 healthy controls matched to 28 chronic pancreatitis patients; 3D-Transit capsule and belt detector over 5 days
Mean +/- 2.2 (not labelled SD or SEM). Gastric emptying 3.1 +/- 1.3 h.
Colonic transit time, healthy controls, electromagnetic capsule
Whole gut transit time, healthy controls, electromagnetic capsule
Total colonic transit time by radiopaque markers
73 healthy persons (24 in the method validation); three marker sets on three days, one film on day 4; men shorter than women (p < 0.05); age and small fibre dose no effect
Mean +/- 2.1 SE (SD about 17.9 h if all 73 contributed, my arithmetic). Segments: right 11.3 +/- 1.1, left 11.4 +/- 1.4, rectosigmoid 12.4 +/- 1.1 h (SE).
Relation of stool form to gastric emptying, small bowel and colonic transit
32 healthy volunteers (12 men), standardised diets, scintigraphy and markers
Value null: the abstract has no transit numbers. Hard stools went with slow colonic transit; stool form could not be related to gastric emptying or small bowel transit.
Fluid passing through the intestinal lumen per day (ingested plus secreted)

Range from the text ('approximately 8-10 L ... every day'). The review gives no split into ingested and secreted volumes (salivary, gastric, biliary, pancreatic, intestinal): those are not on the page.
Fluid left for the colon to absorb per day
'approximately 1.5 L'. No colonic absorption capacity is stated on the page.
Water lost in stool per day

'approximately 100 mL'. Compare the faecal water of Rose 2015 (about 96 g/day from 128 g wet at 75% water) in the excreta table: the two agree to within the rounding of the review, which gives no population.
Capacity of the human colon to absorb fluid
Value null: the PubMed record has no abstract and the Europe PMC record carries none, so no capacity figure was read.

87.5% with 42 g almonds a day and 85.5% with 84 g. Apparent (faecal) digestibility, so it includes bacterial mass and endogenous losses.
